title: Transformers as Intrinsic Optimizers for Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm
authors: Kuan-Cheng Chen, Xiaotian Xu, Hiromichi Matsuyama, Wei-Hao Huang, Haomu Yuan, Yu Yamashiro
abstract: The Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is a leading variational framework for combinatorial optimization on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware, but its practical performance depends strongly on the classical optimizer used to train its variational parameters. This outer-loop optimization is often nonconvex, initialization-sensitive, and costly when repeated across large families of related problem instances. In this work, we propose a Transformer-based intrinsic optimization framework for QAOA, in which the optimizer itself is learned and embedded directly into the hybrid quantum-classical loop. The proposed graph-conditioned Transformer processes problem structure, current QAOA parameters, measurement feedback, and recent optimization history to predict the next variational-parameter update, thereby reformulating instance-wise classical optimization as an amortized learned policy. We develop a mathematical formulation of this intrinsic-optimization perspective and evaluate the method on QAOA-based MaxCut benchmarks across multiple problem settings, with comparisons against representative classical and learned optimization baselines. The results demonstrate that Transformer-based intrinsic optimization can provide a structured and transferable mechanism for improving the classical component of hybrid quantum optimization algorithms.
summary: This paper introduces a novel Transformer-based intrinsic optimizer to overcome the limitations of classical optimization within the QAOA framework for quantum computing. By learning the parameter updates directly from the optimization history, the method transforms the difficult outer-loop optimization into a structured, learned policy. This significantly enhances the performance and transferability of QAOA for solving hard combinatorial problems like MaxCut.
main_problem: The classical optimization loop required for training the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) is nonconvex, sensitive to initialization, and computationally expensive.
main_result: A Transformer-based intrinsic optimization framework successfully learns the parameter updates, significantly outperforming conventional and learned baselines across various MaxCut benchmarks.
method: The authors embed the optimizer directly into the hybrid loop, using a Transformer to process the problem structure, current parameters, and optimization history to predict the next parameter update as an amortized learned policy.
model_or_system: The work focuses on QAOA, a variational quantum algorithm used for combinatorial optimization, specifically applied to the MaxCut problem on graph instances. The optimization involves finding parameters $	heta$ that maximize the expectation value of the cost Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Approximation Ratio (AR) and Mean Energy are the primary metrics used to quantify the quality of the optimized solution.
important_parameters: QAOA depth ($p$), graph size ($n$), and the dimensions of the Transformer model ($d, L$) are varied to test scalability and robustness.
main_assumptions: The performance gain is attributed to the structured, learned update mechanism provided by the Transformer, rather than simply increasing the circuit depth or using better classical optimizers.
figures_summary: Figures demonstrate that the Transformer optimizer achieves superior AR compared to baselines across varying QAOA depths and graph sizes, and that the performance gain is substantial compared to a zero-update control.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitations of standard QAOA optimization. It then details the Transformer architecture, including state tokenization and the prediction head. The core of the work involves formulating the meta-training objective and benchmarking the full system against multiple classical and learned optimizers.
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum algorithms with advanced machine learning techniques, providing a concrete, data-driven method to improve the practical utility of variational quantum algorithms for optimization problems.

figures.caption: Fig. 1: Schematic of the proposed Transformer-based intrinsic optimizer for QAOA on MaxCut. The graph instance G defines the cost Hamiltonian and provides topological input to the learned optimizer. Measurement feedback from the QAOA circuit is encoded in the optimizer state s(t), processed by a Transformer encoder, and decoded into a projected parameter update that produces θ(t+1).

Fig. 2: Training-, validation-, and test-set approximation ratios as functions of the training dataset size for the pro- posed Transformer-based intrinsic optimizer. Shaded regions indicate the standard deviation over five independent random seeds.

Fig. 3: Mean approximation ratio versus number of qubits for the proposed Transformer-based intrinsic optimizer and representative baselines. Shaded regions indicate the corre- sponding standard deviation across benchmark instances.

Fig. 4: Approximation ratio as a function of QAOA circuit depth for the proposed Transformer-based intrinsic optimizer. Curves correspond to training, validation, and test perfor- mance, and the shaded regions indicate the standard deviation over five independent runs with different random seeds.

Fig. 5: Comprehensive benchmarking of the proposed Transformer-based intrinsic optimizer against learned and conventional baselines on unseen MaxCut instances for the case of n = 11 vertices, equivalently 11 qubits, and QAOA depth p = 2. (a) Reports the mean approximation ratio with standard-deviation error bars. (b) Shows the per-instance approximation ratio across benchmark graphs, illustrating the relative robustness and consistency of each method.
